stories.title: Building a Modern B2B Supply Chain from Fergana
stories.author: Azizbek Rahimov
stories.excerpt: How three university students in Fergana built a real-time agricultural supply chain platform connecting 400+ regional farmers directly with commercial buyers.
stories.content:
When we started building in Fergana, the prevailing advice was clear: move to Tashkent immediately or give up. But the problem we were solving—fragmented agricultural logistics and erratic pricing—was happening right in our hometown in the Fergana Valley.

The Regional Advantage

Being 300 kilometers away from the capital forced us to build with extreme operational discipline. We spent our mornings in cold-storage warehouses and our afternoons writing Python backends. Our first 50 customers were people we met at regional produce terminals.

"You don't need a fancy office in the capital to validate customer pain. You need empathy, speed, and relentless follow-through."

Finding the Network

Connecting with Founders Community Uzbekistan gave us access to mentors who helped us structure our first commercial agreements and avoid critical cap-table mistakes. Today, our software processes millions in transactions monthly, and our engineering team remains proud to build from Fergana.

stories.title: Why Central Asia's Next Generation is Choosing Startups Over Corporate Ladders
stories.author: Madina Karimova
stories.excerpt: An analysis of how demographic dividends, mobile internet penetration, and peer-to-peer founder networks are igniting high-velocity venture building across Uzbekistan.
stories.content:
Uzbekistan has one of the youngest populations in Eurasia: over 60% of the country is under the age of 30. For decades, the default career aspirational path for top STEM graduates was corporate employment or civil service. That trajectory is undergoing a seismic shift.

The Peer Effect

When young engineers see peers their own age launch real products that handle thousands of daily transactions, the mental ceiling breaks. Entrepreneurship transitions from an abstract Silicon Valley fairy tale into an accessible craft.

Closing the Information Gap

The remaining bottleneck has never been talent—it has always been high-density access to operational knowledge: how to run customer interviews, how to write clean convertible notes, how to pitch effectively without corporate buzzwords. That is precisely the infrastructure Founders Community is building brick by brick.

stories.title: From Samarkand Hackathon to Seed Funding: The Path of CodeCraft
stories.author: Sherzod Alimov
stories.excerpt: A weekend prototype built at a regional meetup that grew into an automated compliance tool trusted by fintechs across Central Asia.
stories.content:
We didn't set out to build a venture-backed company. We just wanted to stop manually reconciling multilingual regulatory filings for local banks. At a Founders Community Samarkand meetup in late 2025, we showed our messy 48-hour prototype to three visiting founders.

Their blunt feedback was invaluable: strip away 80% of the features and double down on instant document extraction. Six months later, we closed our first pre-seed check and signed contracts with 4 major institutions.
